title: Reaching rejection gives a rejecting halt
statement: Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input symbols, let a computation mode, input bit string $y$, register bound $B$, control label $l$, and register valuation $v$ be given. Suppose the codec machine determined by $N$ and the mode reaches its rejection label from configuration $(l,v)$, with all intermediate configurations satisfying the execution guard, and suppose every register in the resulting valuation $v'$ is at most $B$. Then the machine halts with answer false from $(l,v)$, with every configuration before halting satisfying that same guard.
hypotheses_covered: A finite nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ with Boolean input symbols
A reachable execution from $(l,v)$ to the rejection label, guarded at every earlier step
Final register valuation $v'$ with every register at most $B$
caveat: The guard includes a machine-specific precondition as well as the register bound; the supplied definitions do not give an informal description of that precondition.
